create2_extension_coverage_check.finding: Read test/letflow/iss0397_join_counters_test.exs lines 165-170 directly: `projection_after_create = Repo.get!(InstanceProjection, instance_id, prefix: schema_name)` is fetched immediately after `Engine.create/2` returns, before any `complete_task/3` call. The assertions `length(cohort_after_create["expected_from_branches"]) == 2` and `cohort_after_create["received_from_branches"] == []` can only be satisfied by insert_instance_projection/8's own write inside create/2's Multi (engine.ex persist/12, ~line 965) -- reconcile_projection/5 (the write site every other test in the suite exercises via complete_task/3 or advance_after_timer_fired/3) is never reached at this point in the test. This is genuine, non-inherited coverage of the create/2 extension.

test_isolation_check.finding: Read all three files' setup code directly. iss0397_join_counters_test.exs and timer_wiring_test.exs both use TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 with a unique slug_prefix and System.unique_integer/1-based unique_name/1 helper for all definition names/idempotency keys/actor ids -- no hardcoded shared ids. snapshot_writer_test.exs provisions its own tenant directly (insert_tenant! + provision_tenant_schema + replay_migrations) with a unique slug via TenantSlugFixture.unique_slug/1, and its provisioned_tenant/0 helper calls `Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` at line 53 -- confirmed directly, not taken on faith. The concurrent test in iss0397_join_counters_test.exs (lines 242-262) launches two genuine Elixir.Task.async processes each calling Engine.complete_task/3 on its own separate connection under :auto sandbox mode, which is real cross-connection concurrency, not two sequential calls. All three files use `async: false` and independent on_exit teardown (schema drop / tenant delete). No shared mutable state found. Tests are self-sufficient -- each test provisions its own tenant/definition/instance from scratch.
